newsitem.title: USA: USDA pegs 97/98 world sugar output at 122.4 MMT.
newsitem.headline: USDA pegs 97/98 world sugar output at 122.4 MMT.

text.p: The U.S. Agriculture Department Tuesday estimated 1997/98 world centrifugal sugar production at 122.4 million tonnes (raw value), up slightly from a revised 122.3 million tonnes seen for 1996/97.
USDA previously pegged 1996/97 world sugar output at 124.0 million tonnes.

In its monthly World Agricultural Production report, USDA said sugar produced from sugarcane was forecast at 86.0 million tonnes in 1997/98, up one percent from last year. It said sugar processed from sugarbeets was forecast at 36.4 million tonnes, off three percent from last season.

India 1997/98 sugar production was forecast at 13.6 million tonnes, down seven percent from last season. USDA pinned the decline on a six percent reduction in the volume of cane cut specifically for centrifugal sugar and slightly lower yields.
USDA said the European Union's sugar forecast for 1997/98 was 17.4 million tonnes down four percent from 18.0 million tonnes for 1996/97.
Sugar output in Brazil was pegged at an all-time high of 14.8 million tonnes in 1997/98, versus 14.7 million tonnes in 1996/97, USDA said.
The department forecast Cuba sugar production would climb to 4.5 million tonnes in 1997/98 from 4.4 million tonnes in 1996/97.
